tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

  CLAIM: The builder's record says no obligation is unproved, but two items of brief obligation 2 are refuted and only conditional variants are proved. The item 'preservation of WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan by every step' fails for transfer: op_preserves excludes transfer, and kstep_preserves is a disjunction. The item 'reachable invariant from S3.init statics under DDSound' is false: reachable_kinv_false refutes it, and reachableDU_kinv proves it only on KStepDU runs. The record therefore presents the obligation as discharged.
  VERDICT: Confirmed, but downgraded from major to minor. Brief obligation 2 names two theorems that are not proved. 'Preservation of WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan by every step' fails for transfer: op_preserves excludes it and kstep_preserves is only a disjunction. 'Reachable invariant from S3.init statics under DDSound' is refuted by reachable_kinv_false. Yet kernel-main.md:113-115 lists no unproved obligation ('None'), so that record is misdescribed. def x7 : PState := { x6 with kern := deriveEff x6.kern 6 [1, 2] .modify }  -- auth 8

def plB10 : Pool := ⟨1, 0, 8, [⟨1, 0, true⟩, ⟨2, 0, false⟩]⟩

example : x9.pools[1]? = some plB := by decide

example : x10.res = [⟨0, 5, 6, .modify, [(7, 0, 0)]⟩] := by decide

theorem x10_reach : PReachI K0 st x10 := by
  have h1 : PReachI K0 st x1 := .step .init (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
    (.kernel (.derive (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
  have h2 : PReachI K0 st x2 := .step h1 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
    (.kernel (.store (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
  have h3 : PReachI K0 st x3 := .step h2 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
    (.newPool (others := []) (Guarded.ok (by decide)))
  have h4 : PReachI K0 st x4 := .step h3 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
    (.allocSlot (.ok (pl := plA) rfl (by decide) rfl rfl))
  have r5 : ResolveStep 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ .modify x4 (.ok x5) :=
    .ok (pl := plA4) (sl := ⟨1, 0, true⟩) rfl (by decide) (by decide) rfl (by decide)
  have h5 : PReachI K0 st x5 := .step h4 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1 (.resolve r5)
  have h6 : PReachI K0 st x6 := .step h5 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
    (.kernel (.release (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
  have h7 : PReachI K0 st x7 := .step h6 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
    (.kernel (.derive (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
  have h8 : PReachI K0 st x8 := .step h7 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
    (.kernel (.store (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
  have h9 : PReachI K0 st x9 := .step h8 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1

/-- The literal D.4(3) / brief guarantee ("freeSlot never succeeds on an entry covered by an active
companion descendant"), over every ghost companion, fails on a PReachI state: pool 1 frees slot
place 1 while companion 6 of pool 0 is active and its active descendant 8 covers place 1. -/
theorem literal_guarantee_fails :
    PReachI K0 st x10 ∧ KInv x10.kern ∧
    (∃ L', FreeSlotStep K0 1 ⟨1, 0, 0⟩ x10 (.ok L')) ∧
    (⟨0, 5, 6, .modify, [(7, 0, 0)]⟩ : Res) ∈ x10.res ∧
    x10.kern.Active 6 ∧ x10.kern.Active 8 ∧ 6 ∈ x10.kern.ancs 8 ∧
    1 ∈ x10.kern.afp 8 ∧ 1 ∈ x10.kern.afp 6 ∧ 1 ∈ footprint x10.kern.P 1 ∧
    x10.pools[0]? = some plA4 ∧ x10.kern.I 1 = .uninit := by
  refine ⟨x10_reach, (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1,
    ⟨_, .ok (pl := plB10) (sl := ⟨1, 0, true⟩) rfl (by decide) (by decide) rfl (by decide)⟩,
    by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide,
    by decide⟩

/-- Two active `Modify` companions of two pools over the same storage. -/
theorem two_modify_companions :
    ∃ L', ResolveStep 1 ⟨1, 0, 0⟩ .modify x10 (.ok L') ∧ PReachI K0 st L' ∧
      L'.res = [⟨0, 5, 6, .modify, [(7, 0, 0)]⟩, ⟨1, 8, 9, .modify, [(10, 0, 0)]⟩] ∧
      L'.kern.Active 6 ∧ L'.kern.Active 9 ∧ L'.kern.afp 6 = [1, 2] ∧ L'.kern.afp 9 = [1, 2] := by
  have hok : ResolveStep 1 ⟨1, 0, 0⟩ .modify x10 (.ok _) :=
    .ok (pl := plB10) (sl := ⟨1, 0, true⟩) rfl (by decide) (by decide) rfl (by decide)
  exact ⟨_, hok, .step x10_reach (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1 (.resolve hok), by decide,
    by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩

end Cx

## 36. Shared Mutation and Internal Administration

An abstraction may keep its metadata in `SharedMutable` storage and modify it through `writeShared` to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts. **Shared mutation of metadata does not, however, grant the right to create, recycle, or terminate exclusive authority over the administered storage.** Such operations require `internal` to be exercisable in `Modify` mode from the value administering the storage.

For every administrative abstraction, including arenas, `HandlePool`, and `DataStack`, **`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on the administering value**. The `writeShared` branch alone is insufficient. Operations issuing, recycling, ending, or invalidating regions must preserve active authorities and dependencies. Allocation through administration shared among simultaneous holders, under an interface not providing such exclusive exercise, cannot be expressed in safe code with only these sequential operations: any synchronized implementation of it belongs to Spec 2. These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel.

## 37. Dependent Values and Persistent References

When a value depends on the validity of other storage, that dependency must be carried by an explicit mechanism. In particular, this model retains:

- joint ownership or legal transfer of the resource;
- **non-escaping** dependent values, governed by `depend`, `store`, `AnchorOrder`, and end-of-use operations; they may survive a call if their anchors come from still-valid caller resources;
- library handles checked for identity and generation upon resolution, which are not authorities by themselves;
- validity durations bound to a frame or context, without a universal system of first-class lifetimes;
- safe abstractions encapsulating, when necessary, unsafe operations and proofs of their obligations.
----
## 89. Handles and Persistent References

In a generation-based pool library abstraction, a handle may contain a logical pool identity, an entry identifier, and a generation. This handle is not, by itself, an access right. Safe resolution temporarily supplies authority when the pool and entry are valid; a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure. These conditions belong to the safe abstraction's contract and do not modify the authority-discipline kernel.

## 90. Global and Called Frame

Global storage is anchored to the base frame, but a called function does not acquire ambient authority to modify it merely by being invoked. To access a global, it receives a derived authority under `enterFrame` conditions and may exercise only its effective modes.

1. Machine (Part III). Relations total and deterministic; interpreters calculable with static obligations and WF as proof arguments; agreement theorems both ways on their domain; admissible-state invariants preserved; P1-P4, no double free, frame lemmas, read-after-write on every included sub-range (§16).
2. Kernel (Parts IV-XIII). Every operation exactly as written, including §63.8 and §77 local self-blocking prevention, §65 store rules (derived authority, free leaf, arrival-state exercisability), §72 parameter-origin rule, §73 reanchoring to the first surviving active origin, §69/§70 end of use and free, pinning rules. 3. Arena (Part XIV). issue_as_kernel, reset_as_kernel (both directions, same arrival state on the kernel part), newArena_as_library (no safety property depends on the guard), arena_reuse_safe, ArenaInv preserved.
4. Refinement (§82). Repr including MM-02 WF; R1, R2, R4, R6 for every kernel operation and derived arena operation; simulation with parameters fixed once per run; freeSound_derived; pinned_address_stable; exclusive_bytes. Decisions to apply: declared disjointness is disjointness of leaves (byte disjointness follows from layout well-formedness); a pointer to an empty region has address = base of the effective anchor's allocation and that allocation as provenance; a region's pointer address is the lowest address among its non-empty leaves; a leaf receiving a reference has pointer size (stated hypothesis, classed types/ABI).
5. HandlePool (contract: v0.4 annex). Composite borrow (companion derived from internal over the whole storage, entries derived from the companion); resolveMany Observe by Observe derivations, distinctness only in Modify; allocSlot/freeSlot require a live pool and Modify on the pool value; newPool requires Uninit storage; freeSlot ends the entry content with endUse effects, preconditions excluding internal and its ancestors; PoolInv = entry disjointness + pool_no_stale_access + transition guarantee that freeSlot never succeeds on an entry covered by an active companion descendant. Theorems: pool_resolve_modify_exclusive, pool_no_stale_access, stale/other-pool/atomicity/distinctness, pool_freeSlot_ends_content under the Modify right.
6. DataStack (contract below, identifier DS-v1). Marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it; push and grow use the derived issue; grow is in place only (same base, extension into the space directly after the block, fail otherwise). Theorems: rewind_rejects_live_above, mark_no_aba (for every removed mark), rewind_keeps_older_marks, grow_same_base, grow_keeps_prefix_init, grow_keeps_prefix_bytes through the refinement.

148:### Obligation 5 (HandlePool)
162:| `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive` | HP:1435: on every `PReach` state, under `DDSound`, `∀ r₁ r₂ ∈ res, r₁.pool = r₂.pool → Active r₁.comp → Active r₂.comp → r₁.mode = .modify → r₁.comp = r₂.comp` | Exists and matches D.2 and Jalon3 §4. Re-prove after items 1, 6 and 8 (`companion_blocks` HP:943 survives; the `pReach_inv` dependency on kernel invariants must be re-established). |
167:### Obligation 6 (DataStack, DS-v1)
184:## 4. Spec problems (with evidence)
188:**P1. Pool slot layout is under-determined, and the choice changes accepted programs.** D.1: "Les slots sont des sous-emplacements deux à deux disjoints, inclus dans `storage`". `newPool(storage, internal)` receives no slot description. The draft picks the direct children (`newPoolEff` HP:116). Example: storage `S = {a: {x, y}, b}`. "Slots = children" gives 2 slots `a, b`, so a third `allocSlot` gives `fail`. "Slots = leaves" gives 3 slots `x, y, b`, so the third gives `ok`. A storage that is a single leaf gives 0 slots under the draft, so every `allocSlot` gives `fail`.
190:**P2. Outcome of `freeSlot` on a free slot whose generation matches.** D.3: "un slot déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité" says it must not succeed, but not whether it gives `fail` or `reject`. Example (`pool_free_entry_handle` HZ:977): on a fresh pool, the fabricated handle `⟨0,0,0⟩` names free slot 0 of generation 0. The draft gives `ok`. The contract excludes `ok`, but `fail` (like `resolve`'s "slot … libre ⇒ fail") and `reject` are both possible readings.
192:**P3. `resolve`: `reject` (no right) vs `fail` (bad handle) when both hold.** The right in D.2 ("exercice légal de `internal` au mode requis") includes the effective mode, which depends on the state. Spec v0 §77 orders the arena's analogous checks as availability `fail` (77.4) **before** the effective-right `reject` (77.5). Jalon3 H31a ("Deux `resolve Modify` simultanés, **quels que soient les handles** : le second `reject`") and the draft (HZ:590, `ResolveStep 0 ⟨0, 1, 7⟩ .modify h31 .reject` with a stale generation 7) put `reject` first. Example: with an active `Modify` companion, `resolve(stale h, Modify)` gives `reject` in the draft and `fail` under the §77 analogy. §58 defers to "the operation's contract", which does not settle it.
195:- (a) D.3 lists only "aucune dépendance utilisable ne serait invalidée, aucune feuille n'est épinglée, et aucune autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors `internal` et ses ancêtres"; the brief says "preconditions excluding internal and its ancestors". O12.3 includes "No place remaining usable after the effect depends on an authority held by `place`, **its root**, …". Example: a pool whose `internal` is the storage root (the `pb` setup HZ:565). If some usable place carries `internal` in `D` through `depend` (O5), the literal O12.3 rejects `freeSlot` (draft `EndUseAnchorOK` MM03:3989, `¬ IsRootOf`), although `freeSlot` leaves `internal` active. Whether the exemption also covers O12.3's root clause is not stated.
198:**P5. D.3 contradicts itself when `dst` lies in the allocated slot.** "Le contenu du slot demeure `Uninit` … l'écriture du handle dans `dst` n'initialise pas le slot" holds only if `dst` lies outside the slot. Unlike O18.2 ("leaf `destination` is not in `region`"), `allocSlot` does not exclude it. Example: a frame with `Modify` on the pool value has `internal` exercisable (§43, holder chain), so it has `HasRight .modify q` for a free-slot leaf `q`. `allocSlot(pool, dst := q)` satisfies every D.3 precondition (usable leaf, not `Init`, no authority held), picks slot `q`, and writes the handle into it: the slot becomes `Init`.
200:**P6. "Les entrées libres sont `Uninit`" (D.1) is not an invariant of the open model.** A frame with `Modify` on the pool value can `derive` from `internal` onto a free slot (O1) and `write3` it (O10). That is the same mechanism as the draft counterexample `pool_inv_not_preserved` HP:1830 (a derive from the companion onto a free entry). A later `allocSlot` then hands out an `Init` slot even if `newPool` required `Uninit` storage. D.4 assigns encapsulation to Spec 9. The property can be stated only as an `allocSlot`/`freeSlot` effect, not as a reachable-state theorem, unless Spec 9 encapsulation is modeled.

content.content:
Le registre d'arbitrages A–J reste une **source de traçabilité externe** ; ces identifiants ne sont pas nécessaires au texte normatif final, et aucune ancienne variante contradictoire ne doit subsister après la contre-analyse. La candidate v0.3 ne modifie pas le modèle MM-02 et n'engage pas le jalon 2 avant validation éditoriale.

# Annexe D — Instance `HandlePool` (non normative, contrat de bibliothèque)

Cette annexe décrit une **instance de bibliothèque** de la discipline MM-03, et non une nouvelle opération primitive du langage. Les noms sont sémantiques. Le contrat doit être reconstruit et vérifié ; les résultats du jalon 3 concernent le modèle exploratoire et ses conditions, **pas** automatiquement les règles corrigées ci-dessous.

## D.1 — Identité, état et stockage

Un handle est une donnée `(poolId, slot, gen)` **sans autorité d'accès intrinsèque**. L'identité logique `poolId` est fraîche et n'est pas réutilisée pendant l'exécution pertinente : détruire puis recréer un pool à la même adresse ne réactive pas un ancien handle. Chaque pool vivant conserve une entrée abstraite `{storage, internal, slots}`, où chaque slot possède `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}`. Les slots sont des sous-emplacements deux à deux disjoints, inclus dans `storage` ; leur métadonnée abstraite est représentée en octets par l'implémentation de bibliothèque.

`storage` peut être local, statique, alloué ou être un bloc issu d'une arène. **`newPool(storage, internal)` exige que toutes les feuilles du stockage d'entrée soient `Uninit`** et doit vérifier la garde unifiée de MM-03.3 §2.7 bis sur les deux registres des abstractions vivantes. Il reprend les autres obligations applicables de `newArena` sans fabriquer ni droits ni initialisation des valeurs de slots. Les entrées libres sont `Uninit` ; leur génération initiale est zéro. Une autorité ne peut être `internal` de deux abstractions vivantes, et une arène ne peut réutiliser l'`internal` d'un pool vivant.

## D.2 — Emprunt composé et résolution

Une résolution réussie dérive **de `internal` une autorité compagne** couvrant toutes les feuilles du stockage du pool, de mode `Observe` ou `Modify`, puis dérive **de cette compagne** une autorité de même mode par entrée résolue. L'autorité d'entrée est une descendante de la compagne, et non une autre dérivation indépendante de `internal`. Les deux sont soumises aux règles ordinaires de modes effectifs, d'exercice, de détention, d'ancrage et de transfert ; aucune permission nouvelle n'est créée.

`resolve(h, Observe | Modify)` vérifie l'identité de pool, la génération et la vivacité du slot **avant toute création d'autorité** : handle d'un autre pool, périmé, slot absent ou libre ⇒ `fail`, sans changement d'état. Une résolution valide exige l'exercice légal de `internal` au mode requis. Une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles compagnes sur l'intégralité du stockage du pool ; des compagnes `Observe` peuvent coexister. Il est impossible de libérer une compagne tant que ses descendantes d'entrée sont actives (O3.2). La propriété d'exclusivité concerne toutes les suites d'opérations admises du noyau, pas seulement deux appels successifs de `resolve`.

`resolveMany(handles, Modify)` crée **une** compagne `Modify` et une autorité `Modify` par entrée. La distinction des slots est vérifiée dynamiquement pour ce lot ; toute identité invalide, génération périmée, entrée libre ou répétition de slot donne `fail` **atomique**, sans création partielle de droits. `resolveMany(handles, Observe)` utilise des dérivations `Observe` de la compagne `Observe`, **sans `split` ni contrôle de distinction** : la répétition du même handle valide est permise. Les `reject` de discipline d'accès restent distincts des `fail` de validation des handles.

`unresolve` libère d'abord toutes les dérivées d'entrée encore actives, puis la compagne. Les règles de `release`, y compris celles qui empêchent la libération en présence de descendants ou d'ancres valides, restent applicables ; le contrat ne supprime pas silencieusement des autorités transférées.

## D.3 — Allocation et fin d'usage de slot

`allocSlot(pool, dst)` exige un pool vivant, l'autorisation d'administration de ses métadonnées, une destination utilisable et libre d'autorité active, non `Init`, apte à recevoir la représentation d'un handle. `fail` si aucun slot libre ; `ok` choisit un slot libre, le rend vivant, conserve sa génération et écrit son handle dans la seule feuille `dst`, selon les obligations de représentation (Spec 4) et d'ABI (Spec 11). **Le contenu du slot demeure `Uninit`** jusqu'à son écriture ; l'écriture du handle dans `dst` n'initialise pas le slot.

`freeSlot(h)` exige un pool **vivant** et `MetaRight`, c'est-à-dire le droit légal d'administration de la valeur pool par `Modify` exerçable ou par mutation `writeShared` admissible de ses métadonnées `SharedMutable`. `fail` si l'identité ou la génération ne correspond pas ; un slot déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité. Pour réussir, la fin logique du contenu doit être admissible : **aucune dépendance utilisable** ne serait invalidée, **aucune feuille n'est épinglée**, et **aucune autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors `internal` et ses ancêtres**. En particulier, aucune descendante active d'une compagne ne doit subsister sur cette entrée. Le contrôle n'interprète pas `internal` comme un emprunt externe empêchant systématiquement le nettoyage de ses propres slots.

L'effet `ok` applique au **contenu** les effets de fin d'usage d'`endUse`, remet les feuilles de l'entrée à `Uninit`, marque l'entrée libre et incrémente sa génération ; **il ne désalloue pas implicitement l'allocation MM-02 du stockage**. Il ne s'agit pas de supposer une invocation de O12 autorisée par simple `MetaRight` : la correspondance des effets et la préservation des invariants sous ce droit constituent une **obligation explicite de reconstruction**, notamment dans les cas `writeShared`.

## D.4 — Invariant corrigé et limites

`PoolInv` exige : (1) les entrées sont deux à deux disjointes et incluses dans le stockage ; (2) aucune autorité d'entrée active ne désigne un slot libre ou une ancienne génération (`pool_no_stale_access`) ; (3) **garantie de transition** : `freeSlot` n'aboutit jamais si une descendante active d'une compagne couvre le slot concerné. La dernière clause concerne le succès des transitions, non une interdiction globale de toutes les dérivations du noyau sur des slots libres. Les dérivations ordinaires issues d'une autorité d'entrée restent permises par le noyau.

Les générations sont des entiers naturels dans le modèle abstrait. Leur débordement ou leur recyclage dans une représentation finie doivent être empêchés par l'implémentation (par exemple retrait définitif d'un slot) ; l'ABI est spécifiée en Spec 11. L'encapsulation qui empêche un client d'accéder directement à une compagne administrative appartient à la Spec 9. Les handles persistants peuvent représenter des liens cycliques ; les résolutions qui en découlent restent temporaires et soumises à MM-03.

**Statut des preuves :** le jalon 3 rapporte `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive`, `pool_no_stale_access`, `pool_resolveMany_atomic`, `pool_resolveMany_distinct`, `pool_freeSlot_ends_content` et `pool_entries_disjoint` sur son brouillon, sous les hypothèses détaillées dans `J3_v0.1.md`. Il rapporte également un contre-exemple à l'ancienne formulation de `pool_inv_preserved`. **Il ne constitue pas encore la preuve** de la nouvelle règle `freeSlot` sous `MetaRight` ni de la totalité du contrat corrigé : ces obligations sont consignées en annexe F.

/-- Ghost well-formedness of the pool layer (auxiliary, not a clause of the contract; HandlePool
v0.4 annex, D.1, D.2): fresh distinct identities, well-formed pools and
resolutions (§38). -/
structure PoolWF (L : PState) : Prop where
  /-- D.1: identities are below the next fresh identity. -/
  ids : ∀ sh ∈ L.pools.map Pool.shape, sh.id < L.nId
  /-- D.1: identities are distinct. -/
  nodup : ((L.pools.map Pool.shape).map (·.id)).Nodup
  /-- D.1: every pool is well formed. -/
  pools : ∀ sh ∈ L.pools.map Pool.shape, PoolOK L.kern sh
  /-- D.2: every ghost resolution is well formed. -/
  res : ∀ r ∈ L.res, ResOK L.kern (L.pools.map Pool.shape) r

/-- `pool_no_stale_access` as a state predicate (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 2; non-normative
library contract): no active entry authority designates a free slot or a former generation (§89). -/
def NoStale (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ r ∈ L.res, ∀ e ∈ r.entries, L.kern.Active e.1 → ∃ pl ∈ L.pools, pl.id = r.pool ∧
    ∃ sl, pl.slots[e.2.1]? = some sl ∧ sl.gen = e.2.2 ∧ sl.live = true

/-- Exclusivity of companions (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; non-normative library contract): two
distinct active companions of a pool are both `Observe` (§43, §50). -/
def CompExcl (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ r₁ ∈ L.res, ∀ r₂ ∈ L.res, r₁.pool = r₂.pool → r₁.comp ≠ r₂.comp →
    L.kern.Active r₁.comp → L.kern.Active r₂.comp → r₁.mode = .observe ∧ r₂.mode = .observe

/-- Footprints of every place with a leaf are kept (§40; support for HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1). -/
def FpKeep (s s' : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ q l₀, l₀ ∈ footprint s.P q → ∀ l, l ∈ footprint s'.P q ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P q

/-- Same places keep footprints (§40). -/
theorem fpKeep_of_P {s s' : S3} (h : s'.P = s.P) : FpKeep s s' := fun _ _ _ _ => by rw [h]

/-- `CompExcl` carries over to a kernel state that reactivates nothing (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2)
(§42). -/
theorem CompExcl.kern {L : PState} {s' : S3} (h : CompExcl L) (hw : PoolWF L)
    (hA : Arena.AKeep L.kern s') : CompExcl { L with kern := s' } :=
  fun r₁ hr₁ r₂ hr₂ hp hne ha₁ ha₂ => h r₁ hr₁ r₂ hr₂ hp hne
    (hA.active_back ha₁ (comp_lt hw hr₁)) (hA.active_back ha₂ (comp_lt hw hr₂))

/-- Two shapes of a list with distinct identities and the same identity are equal (HandlePool v0.4
annex, D.1; §46). -/
theorem eq_of_id : ∀ {l : List PoolShape} {a b : PoolShape}, (l.map (·.id)).Nodup → a ∈ l →
    b ∈ l → a.id = b.id → a = b
  | [], _, _, _, ha, _, _ => by simp at ha
  | c :: l, a, b, hn, ha, hb, he => by
    rw [List.map_cons, List.nodup_cons] at hn
    rcases List.mem_cons.1 ha with ha' | ha' <;> rcases List.mem_cons.1 hb with hb' | hb'
    · rw [ha', hb']
    · subst ha'; exact absurd (he ▸ List.mem_map_of_mem (f := (·.id)) hb') hn.1
    · subst hb'; exact absurd (he.symm ▸ List.mem_map_of_mem (f := (·.id)) ha') hn.1
    · exact eq_of_id hn.2 ha' hb' he

/-- The ghost resolution of pool `pl` names its `internal` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §38). -/
theorem res_internal {L : PState} (hw : PoolWF L) {r : Res} (hr : r ∈ L.res) {pl : Pool}
    (hpl : pl ∈ L.pools) (hp : r.pool = pl.id) :
    r.internal = pl.internal ∧ r.internal < r.comp ∧
      (∀ e ∈ r.entries, r.comp < e.1 ∧ ∃ q, (pl.slots.map (·.place))[e.2.1]? = some q ∧
        OptP (L.kern.A[e.1]?) (fun y => ∀ l, l ∈ y.footprint ↔ l ∈ footprint L.kern.P q) False) ∧
      OptP (L.kern.A[r.comp]?) (fun y => y.mode = r.mode ∧
        ∀ l, l ∈ y.footprint ↔ l ∈ footprint L.kern.P pl.storage) False := by
  obtain ⟨sh, hsh, hid, hint, hlt, hc, he⟩ := hw.res r hr
  have e : sh = pl.shape :=
    eq_of_id hw.nodup hsh (List.mem_map_of_mem hpl) (hid.trans hp)
  subst e
  exact ⟨hint.symm, hlt, he, hc⟩

/-! ## Preservation of the ghost invariants (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1–D.4) -/

/-- An active companion of a pool and a new companion are both `Observe` (HandlePool v0.4 annex,
D.2: "Une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles compagnes … ; des compagnes `Observe`
peuvent coexister"): an active companion unrelated to `internal` contradicts I1 (§50), since
`internal` is `Modify`; a descendant takes away the effective mode that the new derivation needs
(§43, §60.2). -/
theorem companion_blocks {s : S3} (hi1 : I1 s) {pl : Pool} {m : Mode} (hR : ResolveRight s pl m)
    (hok : PoolOK s pl.shape) {c : Nat} {y : Authority} (hc : s.A[c]? = some y)
    (ya : y.active = true) (hlt : pl.internal < c)

    y.mode = .observe ∧ m = .observe := by

  obtain ⟨xi, hxi, xa⟩ := hR.active
  obtain ⟨xi', hxi', hmi⟩ := optP_false_iff.1 hok.internalMode
  have e : xi' = xi := Option.some.inj (hxi'.symm.trans hxi)
  subst e
  have hli : l ∈ xi'.footprint := by have := hR.within l hl; simpa [S3.afp, hxi] using this
  have hly : l ∈ y.footprint := (hfp l).2 hl
  have hz : pl.internal ∈ s.ancs c := Decidable.byContradiction fun hn => by
    have hn2 : c ∉ s.ancs pl.internal := fun h => absurd (chain_lt h) (by omega)
    have := hi1 pl.internal c xi' y l (by omega) hxi hc xa ya hli hly hn hn2
    rw [hmi] at this; cases this.1
  have hal := hR.modeOK l hl
  rw [effective_eq hxi xa hli] at hal
  have hd : y.mode ∈ descModes s pl.internal l := mem_descModes.2 ⟨c, y, hc, ya, hly, hz, rfl⟩
  rcases allows_effOf hal with ⟨h0, -⟩ | ⟨hn, rfl⟩
  · rw [h0] at hd; cases hd
  · exact ⟨mode_eq_observe fun e => hn (e ▸ hd), rfl⟩

/-- A new resolution of pool `pl`, made under `ResolveRight`, keeps `CompExcl` (HandlePool v0.4
annex, D.2; §43, §50, §60). -/

/-- The invariants of library runs (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1–D.4; §57): on every state reached
by steps from states satisfying `KInv`, the kernel state is reached by kernel steps and ends of slot
contents, and the ghost invariants hold. -/
theorem pReachI_inv {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    XReach k statics L.kern ∧ PoolWF L ∧ NoStale L ∧ CompExcl L := by
  induction h with
  | init =>
    refine ⟨.init, ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> simp [PState.init, NoStale, CompExcl]
  | step _ hk hs ih =>
    obtain ⟨hr, hwf, hns, hce⟩ := ih
    exact ⟨xreach_pstep hr hk hs, pstep_inv hk.1 hk.2.1.1.1 hwf hns hce hs⟩

/-- Under the guarantee of §57 (`KernelGuarantee`), every library-reachable state is reached by
steps from states satisfying `KInv` (HandlePool v0.4 annex). -/
theorem PReach.toI {k : K} {statics : Statics} (hX : KernelGuarantee k statics) {L : PState}
    (h : PReach k statics L) : PReachI k statics L := by
  have hxr := pReach_xreach hX h
  induction h with
  | init => exact .init
  | step hr hs ih => exact .step (ih (pReach_xreach hX hr)) (hX _ (pReach_xreach hX hr)) hs

/-! ## `PoolInv` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4) -/

/-- `PoolInv`, item 1 (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4; non-normative library contract): the entries of
every pool lie in its storage and are pairwise disjoint (§40). -/
def EntriesDisjoint (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ pl ∈ L.pools,
    (∀ sl ∈ pl.slots, ∀ l ∈ footprint L.kern.P sl.place, l ∈ footprint L.kern.P pl.storage) ∧
    ∀ (a b : Nat) (sa sb : Slot), pl.slots[a]? = some sa → pl.slots[b]? = some sb → a ≠ b →
      ∀ l ∈ footprint L.kern.P sa.place, l ∉ footprint L.kern.P sb.place

/-- `PoolInv`, item 3, the transition guarantee (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4; non-normative library
contract): `freeSlot` never succeeds while an active descendant of a companion of the pool covers
the slot concerned (§43, §69). -/
def FreeGuarantee (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (L' : PState), FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L') →
    ∀ (pl : Pool) (sl : Slot), L.pools[j]? = some pl → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      ∀ r ∈ L.res, r.pool = pl.id → ∀ x, L.kern.Active x → (x = r.comp ∨ r.comp ∈ L.kern.ancs x) →
        ∀ l ∈ L.kern.afp x, l ∉ footprint L.kern.P sl.place

/-- `PoolInv` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, as corrected; non-normative library contract): entry
disjointness, `pool_no_stale_access`, and the transition guarantee of `freeSlot` (§55, §57). -/
def PoolInv (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop := EntriesDisjoint L ∧ NoStale L ∧ FreeGuarantee k L

/-- `EntriesDisjoint` follows from the ghost well-formedness (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 1)
(§40). -/
theorem entriesDisjoint_of {L : PState} (hwf : PoolWF L) : EntriesDisjoint L := by
  intro pl hpl
  have hok := hwf.pools _ (List.mem_map_of_mem hpl)
  exact ⟨fun sl hsl l hl => hok.slotIn sl.place (List.mem_map_of_mem (f := (·.place)) hsl) l hl,
    fun a b sa sb ha hb hab => hok.disjoint a b sa.place sb.place
      (by simp [Pool.shape, ha]) (by simp [Pool.shape, hb]) hab⟩

/-- The transition guarantee follows from the ghost well-formedness (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4,
item 3): an active descendant of a companion of the pool is younger than `internal`, so it is
neither `internal` nor one of its ancestors, and `ContentEndPre` forbids it to cover the entry (§43,
§69). -/
theorem freeGuarantee_of {k : K} {L : PState} (hwf : PoolWF L) : FreeGuarantee k L := by
  intro j h L' hst pl sl hpj hsl r hr hrp x hx hxr l hl hlq
  cases hst with
  | @ok pl' sl' hpj' _ _ hsl' hpre =>
    rw [hpj] at hpj'; cases hpj'
    rw [hsl] at hsl'; cases hsl'
    obtain ⟨hint, hlt, -, -⟩ := res_internal hwf hr (List.mem_of_getElem? hpj) hrp
    obtain ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ := hx
    have hex := hpre.entry x (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy)) ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ ⟨l, hl, hlq⟩
    have hcx : r.comp ≤ x := by
      rcases hxr with rfl | hc
      · exact Nat.le_refl _
      · exact Nat.le_of_lt (chain_lt hc)
    unfold Exempt at hex
    rcases hex with rfl | h'
    · omega
    · have := chain_lt h'; omega

/-- `pool_inv_preserved` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4): `PoolInv` holds on every state of a library
run whose steps start from states satisfying `KInv` (§57); with `PReach.toI`, on every
library-reachable state under the guarantee of §57. -/
theorem pool_inv_preserved {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    PoolInv k L :=
  have ⟨_, hwf, hns, _⟩ := pReachI_inv h
  ⟨entriesDisjoint_of hwf, hns, freeGuarantee_of hwf⟩

/-- `pool_entries_disjoint` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 1; §40). -/
theorem pool_entries_disjoint {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    EntriesDisjoint L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved h).1

/-- `pool_no_stale_access` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 2): on every state of a library run
(`PReachI`), an active entry authority designates a live slot at its current generation (§89). -/
theorem pool_no_stale_access {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    NoStale L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved h).2.1

/-- `pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 3): on every state of a
library run (`PReachI`), `freeSlot` never succeeds while an active descendant of a companion of the
pool covers the slot (§43, §69). -/
theorem pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) : FreeGuarantee k L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved h).2.2

/-- `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2: "La propriété d'exclusivité
concerne toutes les suites d'opérations admises du noyau"): on every state of a library run
(`PReachI`), whatever its kernel steps, an active `Modify` companion of a pool is its only active
companion (§43, §50). -/
theorem pool_resolve_modify_exclusive {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    ∀ r₁ ∈ L.res, ∀ r₂ ∈ L.res, r₁.pool = r₂.pool → L.kern.Active r₁.comp →
      L.kern.Active r₂.comp → r₁.mode = .modify → r₁.comp = r₂.comp := by
  intro r₁ hr₁ r₂ hr₂ hp ha₁ ha₂ hm
  refine Decidable.byContradiction fun hne => ?_
  have := (pReachI_inv h).2.2.2 r₁ hr₁ r₂ hr₂ hp hne ha₁ ha₂
  rw [hm] at this; cases this.1

/-! ## Handle validation: stale, other pool, free slot (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2, D.3; §89) -/

/-- A handle of another pool is not valid (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2, D.3; §89). -/
theorem not_handleOK_other {pl : Pool} {h : Handle} (hid : h.id ≠ pl.id) : ¬ HandleOK pl h :=
  fun ⟨e, _⟩ => hid e

Runs from `PState.init Witness.hst` under the test contract `Examples.K0` (§48). Statics (§47):
place 0 is the pool storage, with two leaf children 1 and 2 (`Uninit`); place 3 is the pool value
(`Init`); place 4 is a destination (`Uninit`); root authorities 0, 1 and 2 cover places 0, 3 and 4.
`internal` is authority 3, derived from 0 over `[1, 2]` and stored in place 3. Every precondition is
decided by `decide`. -/

namespace Witness

open Examples

/-- Statics of the witnesses (§47; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1). -/
def hst : Statics :=
  [((none, none, 0), false), ((some 0, none, 0), false), ((some 0, none, 0), false),
    ((none, none, 0), true), ((none, none, 0), false)]

/-- Initial library state (§47). -/
def w0 : PState := PState.init hst

/-- After `derive(0, [1, 2], Modify)` (§60): authority 3, the future `internal`. -/
def w1 : PState := { w0 with kern := deriveEff w0.kern 0 [1, 2] .modify }

/-- After `store(3, 3)` (§65): `internal` is held by the pool value, place 3. -/
def w2 : PState := { w1 with kern := storeEff w1.kern 3 3 }

/-- After `newPool(0, 3)` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1): pool 0 with slots 1 and 2, free, of
generation 0 (§47). -/
def w3 : PState := newPoolEff w2 0 3

/-- Pool 0 after `newPool` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §47). -/
def pl3 : Pool := ⟨0, 0, 3, [⟨1, 0, false⟩, ⟨2, 0, false⟩]⟩

/-- After `allocSlot(0, 4)` on slot 0 (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3): the handle `⟨0, 0, 0⟩` is
written into place 4 (§47, §67). -/
def w4 : PState := allocSlotEff w3 0 pl3 0 ⟨1, 0, false⟩ 4

/-- Pool 0 after `allocSlot` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §47). -/
def pl4 : Pool := ⟨0, 0, 3, [⟨1, 0, true⟩, ⟨2, 0, false⟩]⟩

/-- `w3` is reached by a library run whose steps start from states satisfying `KInv` (§57, §60,
§65; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1). -/
theorem w3_reach : PReachI K0 hst w3 :=
  .step (.step (.step .init (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
    (.kernel (.derive (Guarded.ok (by decide))))) (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
    (.kernel (.store (Guarded.ok (by decide))))) (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
    (.newPool (others := []) (Guarded.ok (by decide)))

/-- `w4` is library-reachable (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §47, §67). -/
theorem w4_reach : PReachI K0 hst w4 :=
  .step w3_reach (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
    (.allocSlot (.ok (pl := pl3) rfl (by decide) rfl rfl))

/-- `resolveMany` in `Observe` accepts a repeated valid handle (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2: "la
répétition du même handle valide est permise"): two `Observe` entry authorities on slot 0, derived
from one `Observe` companion; the same batch in `Modify` fails (§60). -/
theorem observe_repeat_ok :
    (∃ L', ResolveManyStep K0 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 0, 0⟩] .observe w4 (.ok L') ∧ PReachI K0 hst L' ∧
      L'.res = [⟨0, 3, 4, .observe, [(5, 0, 0), (6, 0, 0)]⟩]) ∧
    ∀ o, ResolveManyStep K0 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 0, 0⟩] .modify w4 o → o = .fail := by
  have hok : ResolveManyStep K0 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 0, 0⟩] .observe w4 (.ok _) :=
    .ok (pl := pl4) rfl (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)
  exact ⟨⟨_, hok, .step w4_reach (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1 (.resolveMany hok), rfl⟩,
    (pool_resolveMany_distinct (L' := w4) (pl := pl4)).1 rfl (by decide) (by decide)⟩

/-- `freeSlot` is not a kernel `endUse` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "Le contrôle n'interprète pas
`internal` comme un emprunt externe"; §69.2): on `w4`, `freeSlot(⟨0, 0, 0⟩)` is accepted, while the
kernel `endUse` of slot place 1 is rejected, because `internal` (authority 3, derived, active,
covering place 1) is held by the pool value outside the slot. Both states satisfy `KInv ∧ KAux`
(§57), decided through `Arena.KInvB`. -/
theorem freeSlot_not_endUse :
    (∃ L', FreeSlotStep K0 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ w4 (.ok L') ∧ PReachI K0 hst L' ∧
      KInv L'.kern ∧ KAux L'.kern) ∧
      ¬ EndUsePre K0 w4.kern 1 ∧ KInv w4.kern ∧ KAux w4.kern := by
  have hok : FreeSlotStep K0 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ w4 (.ok _) :=
    .ok (pl := pl4) (sl := ⟨1, 0, true⟩) rfl (by decide) (by decide) rfl (by decide)
  have hk4 : KInv w4.kern ∧ KAux w4.kern := Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)
  exact ⟨⟨_, hok, .step w4_reach hk4.1 (.freeSlot hok), Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)⟩, by decide,
    hk4⟩

/-- Contract problem (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "Le contenu du slot demeure `Uninit` jusqu'à son
écriture ; l'écriture du handle dans `dst` n'initialise pas le slot"): the preconditions of
`allocSlot` do not exclude a destination inside the allocated slot. On `w3`, `allocSlot(0, 1)` is
accepted on slot 0, whose place is 1: the slot becomes live and its content `Init` (§67). -/
theorem allocSlot_into_own_slot :
    ∃ L', AllocSlotStep 0 1 w3 (.ok L') ∧ PReachI K0 hst L' ∧
      L'.pools[0]? = some pl4 ∧ L'.kern.I 1 = .init := by
  have hok : AllocSlotStep 0 1 w3 (.ok (allocSlotEff w3 0 pl3 0 ⟨1, 0, false⟩ 1)) :=
    .ok rfl (by decide) rfl rfl
  exact ⟨_, hok, .step w3_reach (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1 (.allocSlot hok), rfl, by decide⟩

/-- Contract problem (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1: "Les entrées libres sont `Uninit`"): free
entries are not `Uninit` in every library-reachable state. On `w3`, a frame with `Modify` over the
pool value derives from `internal` over slot place 1 (O1, §60) and writes it (O10, §67): slot 0
stays free while its content is `Init`. -/
theorem free_slot_init :
    ∃ L, PReachI K0 hst L ∧ L.pools[0]? = some pl3 ∧ L.kern.I 1 = .init := by
  have h₁ : PStep K0 w3 { w3 with kern := deriveEff w3.kern 3 [1] .modify } :=
    .kernel (.derive (Guarded.ok (by decide)))
  have h₂ : PStep K0 { w3 with kern := deriveEff w3.kern 3 [1] .modify }
      { w3 with kern := write3Eff (deriveEff w3.kern 3 [1] .modify) [1] } :=
    .kernel (.write (a := 4) (Guarded.ok (by decide)))
  exact ⟨_, .step (.step w3_reach (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1 h₁)
    (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1 h₂, rfl, by decide⟩

end Witness

# Handle pool: a library instance of the access discipline (non-normative)

**Non-normative.** This module formalizes the library contract "HandlePool v0.4 annex" (items
D.1–D.4), which `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md` does not define (§75, Part XIV
preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and
are not defined here"). The normative clauses that constrain it are
§36 (`MetaRight` is exercisable `Modify` on the administering value; `writeShared` alone is
insufficient), §37 and §89 (handles are data, not authorities), §38 and §46 (library state outside
`S₃`), §47 (empty initial registry), §56 (the guard over all registries of live administrations)
and §58 (outcomes, statics before `fail`).

The pool registry lives beside the kernel state (`PState`). Its operations are built on the
kernel operations O1–O16 (§60–§75): `newPool` registers only; `allocSlot` writes the handle into
its destination (O10); `resolve` derives a companion from `internal` over the whole storage, then
an entry authority from the companion (O1 twice); `resolveMany` does the same with `split` (O2) in
`Modify` and with one `Observe` derive per handle (O1) in `Observe`; `unresolve` releases (O3).
`freeSlot` applies the effect function of O12 (§69) to the slot content under preconditions that
exempt `internal` and its ancestors (`ContentEndPre`): it is not a kernel `endUse` step.
`contentEnd_preserves` proves that it preserves `KInv ∧ KAux` (§57); `pstep_kernel` states what
every pool step is on the kernel side.
-/

[is] not defined here" (mapping P0). Every definition below that goes beyond §36/§37/§38/§46/§47/§56/
§58/§89 encodes the non-normative contract.

Machine-checked witnesses are in the `Witness` namespace of the module (decided by `decide`).

leaves give `x, y, b` (third `allocSlot` → `ok`). A storage that is a leaf has no slot: every
`allocSlot` gives `fail`.

**H-R2 (mapping P2). `freeSlot` of a free slot whose identity and generation match.** D.3: "un slot
déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité" (excludes `ok`, does not say which
outcome). Used: `fail` (same handle validation `HandleOK` as `resolve`, D.2 "slot … libre ⇒ `fail`").
Alternative: `reject`. Example: fresh pool, `freeSlot(⟨id, 0, 0⟩)` on free slot 0: `fail` (used) vs
`reject`. Theorem `pool_freeSlot_stale_other_free_fails`.

**H-R3 (mapping P3). `resolve`/`resolveMany`/`freeSlot`: right before handle validity.** D.2 orders
handle validation "avant toute création d'autorité", not against the right; §58 "according to the
operation's contract". Used (draft): `reject` without the right (`ResolveRight` = `DerivePre` of the
companion; `AdminRight` for `freeSlot`), then `fail` for an invalid handle. Alternative (§77
analogy): handle `fail` first. Example: with an active `Modify` companion, `resolve(stale h, Modify)`:

**H-R4. Missing pool index.** D.2/D.3 do not say what `resolve`, `resolveMany`, `allocSlot`, `freeSlot`

/-- Library states reachable from the initial library state (§47) by library steps (HandlePool v0.4
annex; non-normative library contract). -/
inductive PReach (k : K) (statics : Statics) : PState → Prop where
  | init : PReach k statics (PState.init statics)
  | step {L L' : PState} : PReach k statics L → PStep k L L' → PReach k statics L'

/-- Library runs in which every step starts from a kernel state satisfying `KInv` (§57; HandlePool
v0.4 annex). Under the guarantee of §57 every library-reachable state is such a state
(`PReach.toI`); the pool theorems are stated on these runs, so that they do not depend on that
guarantee. -/
inductive PReachI (k : K) (statics : Statics) : PState → Prop where
  | init : PReachI k statics (PState.init statics)
  | step {L L' : PState} : PReachI k statics L → KInv L.kern → PStep k L L' →
      PReachI k statics L'

/-- Kernel side of library runs (§57, §69 effect; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3): a kernel step
O1–O16, or the end of the content of a slot place `q` under `ContentEndPre` for some `internal`
`i`. -/
inductive XStep (k : K) : S3 → S3 → Prop where
  | kernel {s s' : S3} : KStep k s s' → XStep k s s'
theorem XReach.kseq {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s s' : S3} (hr : XReach k statics s)
    (h : KSeq k s s') : XReach k statics s' := by
  induction h with
  | refl => exact hr
  | tail _ hs ih => exact .step ih (.kernel hs)

/-- The guarantee of §57 on the kernel side of library runs (HandlePool v0.4 annex): `KInv` on
every state reached by kernel steps O1–O16 and ends of slot contents. It is not a clause of the
contract and is not proved here: `xreach_inv` reduces it to the preservation of `KInv ∧ KAux` by
every kernel step, which the transfer of §63 breaks (`transfer_breaks_kinv`). -/
def KernelGuarantee (k : K) (statics : Statics) : Prop := ∀ s, XReach k statics s → KInv s

/-- A library step from a kernel state in `XReach` lands in `XReach`, under `KInv` (§57;
HandlePool v0.4 annex). -/
theorem xreach_pstep {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L L' : PState}
    (hr : XReach k statics L.kern) (hk : KInv L.kern) (hs : PStep k L L') :
    XReach k statics L'.kern := by
  rcases pstep_kernel hk hs with h | ⟨q, i, hpre, he⟩
  · exact hr.kseq h
  · rw [he]; exact .step hr (.contentEnd hpre)

/-- The kernel state of every library-reachable state is reached from `S3.init statics` by kernel
steps O1–O16 and ends of slot contents (§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex), given `KInv` on such
states. -/
theorem pReach_xreach {k : K} {statics : Statics} (hX : KernelGuarantee k statics)
    {L : PState} (h : PReach k statics L) : XReach k statics L.kern := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact .init
  | step _ hs ih => exact xreach_pstep ih (hX _ ih) hs

/-- `KInv ∧ KAux` (§57) holds on every state reached by kernel steps and ends of slot contents,
when it holds initially and every kernel step O1–O16 preserves it (`contentEnd_preserves` covers the
ends of slot contents; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3). -/
theorem xreach_inv {k : K} {statics : Statics}
    (h0 : KInv (S3.init statics) ∧ KAux (S3.init statics))
    (hK : ∀ s s', KInv s → KAux s → KStep k s s' → KInv s' ∧ KAux s') {s : S3}
    (h : XReach k statics s) : KInv s ∧ KAux s := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact h0
  | step _ hs ih =>
    cases hs with
    | kernel hs => exact hK _ _ ih.1 ih.2 hs
    | contentEnd hpre => exact contentEnd_preserves ih.1 ih.2 hpre

inductive ResolveStep (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (m : Mode) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → ResolveStep j h m L .reject
  | noRight {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ ResolveRight L.kern pl m →
      ResolveStep j h m L .reject
  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight L.kern pl m → ¬ HandleOK pl h →
      ResolveStep j h m L .fail
  | noEntry {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight L.kern pl m →
      HandleOK pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      ¬ DerivePre (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (footprint L.kern.P sl.place) m →
      ResolveStep j h m L .reject
  | ok {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight L.kern pl m →
      HandleOK pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      DerivePre (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (footprint L.kern.P sl.place) m →
      ResolveStep j h m L (.ok { L with
        kern := deriveEff (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (footprint L.kern.P sl.place) m
        res := L.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, L.kern.A.length, m,
          [(L.kern.A.length + 1, h.slot, h.gen)]⟩] })

/-- Validity of a batch (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; non-normative library contract): every handle
designates a live slot at its generation; pairwise distinct slots in `Modify` only (§58, §89). -/
      UnresolveStep c L (.ok { L with kern := s' })

/-! ## `freeSlot` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3) -/

/-- `x` is exempt from the end-of-use checks of a slot of the pool of `internal` `i`: `internal` or
one of its ancestors (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "hors `internal` et ses ancêtres"; non-normative
library contract; §69). -/
def Exempt (s : S3) (i x : Nat) : Prop := x = i ∨ x ∈ s.ancs i

/-- Decidability of `Exempt` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §69). -/
instance (s : S3) (i x : Nat) : Decidable (Exempt s i x) := by unfold Exempt; infer_instance

/-- §69.2 for storage that dies with the content (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: the end-of-use
effects of O12; non-normative library contract): an active derived authority over a leaf of a place
that stops being usable is held within the slot `q` or by a dying holder. -/
def DyingAccessOK (s : S3) (q j : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun y => y.active = true → y.origin ≠ none →
    (∃ l ∈ y.footprint, isLeaf s.P l ∧ s.Usable l ∧ ¬ (endUseS s q).Usable l) →
      heldIn s.P q y.holder ∨ ¬ HolderLive (endUseS s q) y.holder) True

/-- Decidability of `DyingAccessOK` (§69.2). -/
instance (s : S3) (q j : Nat) : Decidable (DyingAccessOK s q j) := by
  unfold DyingAccessOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- §69.3 with the exemption of D.3 (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative library contract):
anchor `x` of a place remaining usable is not held within the slot `q` and keeps a live holder;
unless exempt, it is not a root of `q`. -/
def ContentAnchorOK (s : S3) (q i x : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => ¬ heldIn s.P q y.holder ∧ (¬ Exempt s i x → ¬ IsRootOf s q y) ∧
    HolderLive (endUseS s q) y.holder) True

/-- Decidability of `ContentAnchorOK` (§69.3). -/
instance (s : S3) (q i x : Nat) : Decidable (ContentAnchorOK s q i x) := by
  unfold ContentAnchorOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of the end of the content of slot place `q` of the pool of `internal` `i`
(HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "la fin logique du contenu doit être admissible"; the preconditions
of O12, §69, excluding `internal` and its ancestors; non-normative library contract). §69.1 is not
a precondition: `freeSlot_modify_right` derives it from `AdminRight`. -/
structure ContentEndPre (k : K) (s : S3) (q i : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- D.3: no active authority covers the entry except `internal` and its ancestors (§69.2 on the
  leaves of the entry, with the exemption). -/
  entry : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active j → (∃ l ∈ s.afp j, l ∈ footprint s.P q) →
    Exempt s i j
  /-- §69.2 on the storage that dies with the content. -/
  dying : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, DyingAccessOK s q j
  /-- D.3, §69.3: no usable dependency is invalidated. -/
  anchors : ∀ q' ∈ List.range s.P.length, (endUseS s q).Usable q' →
    ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s q).D q', ContentAnchorOK s q i x
  /-- D.3, §69.4: no ending leaf is pinned, statically or dynamically. -/
  notPinned : ∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, EndingLeaf s q l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l

/-- Decidability of `ContentEndPre` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §69). -/
instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (q i : Nat) :
    Decidable (ContentEndPre k s q i) :=
  decidable_of_iff ((∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active j →
      (∃ l ∈ s.afp j, l ∈ footprint s.P q) → Exempt s i j) ∧
    (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, DyingAccessOK s q j) ∧
    (∀ q' ∈ List.range s.P.length, (endUseS s q).Usable q' →
      ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s q).D q', ContentAnchorOK s q i x) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, EndingLeaf s q l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l))
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c, d⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d⟩⟩

/-- Effect of `freeSlot` on slot `i` of pool `j` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative library
contract): the effects of O12 on the slot content (`endUseEff`, §69), no deallocation; the slot
becomes free and its generation is incremented. -/
def freeSlotEff (L : PState) (j : Nat) (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) : PState :=
  { L with
    kern := endUseEff L.kern sl.place
    pools := L.pools.set j (setSlot pl i ⟨sl.place, sl.gen + 1, false⟩) }

/-- `freeSlot(h)` on pool `j` as a relation (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3, corrected by §36; §58;
non-normative library contract): `reject` without the pool, without a live pool or `MetaRight`;
then `fail` for a handle of another pool, stale, absent or free; then `reject` unless the end of
the content is admissible (`ContentEndPre`). -/
inductive FreeSlotStep (k : K) (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → FreeSlotStep k j h L .reject
  | noRight {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ AdminRight L.kern pl →
      FreeSlotStep k j h L .reject
  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AdminRight L.kern pl → ¬ HandleOK pl h →
      FreeSlotStep k j h L .fail
  | noEnd {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AdminRight L.kern pl →
      HandleOK pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → ¬ ContentEndPre k L.kern sl.place pl.internal →
      FreeSlotStep k j h L .reject
  | ok {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AdminRight L.kern pl →
      HandleOK pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → ContentEndPre k L.kern sl.place pl.internal →
      FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok (freeSlotEff L j pl h.slot sl))

/-! ## Library runs (HandlePool v0.4 annex; §38, §46, §57) -/

/-- One `ok` step of a library run (HandlePool v0.4 annex; non-normative library contract): a
kernel step O1–O16 of non-administrative code, the registry unchanged, or an accepted pool
operation (§57, §58). -/
inductive PStep (k : K) : PState → PState → Prop where
  | kernel {L : PState} {s' : S3} : KStep k L.kern s' → PStep k L { L with kern := s' }
  | newPool {L L' : PState} {others : List (List Nat)} {st i : Nat} :

/-- `PoolInv`, item 3, the transition guarantee, as the contract states it (HandlePool v0.4 annex,
D.4: "`freeSlot` n'aboutit jamais si une descendante active d'une compagne couvre le slot
concerné"; non-normative library contract): `freeSlot` never succeeds while an active strict
descendant of a companion covers the slot concerned (§43, §69). The contract does not restrict the
companion to the pool of the slot. This guarantee is false on a library-reachable state
(`Witness.pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_false`): D.3 exempts "`internal` et ses ancêtres", which
may include a companion of another pool. -/
def FreeGuarantee (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (L' : PState), FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L') →
    ∀ (pl : Pool) (sl : Slot), L.pools[j]? = some pl → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      ∀ r ∈ L.res, ∀ x, L.kern.Active x → r.comp ∈ L.kern.ancs x →
        ∀ l ∈ L.kern.afp x, l ∉ footprint L.kern.P sl.place

/-- Same-pool restriction of the transition guarantee (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 3;
non-normative library contract). This is not the contract's statement (`FreeGuarantee`): only the
companions of the slot's pool are quantified (`r.pool = pl.id`). On that point it is weaker; it also
covers the companion itself, and on that point it is stronger (§43, §69). -/
def FreeGuaranteeSamePool (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (L' : PState), FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L') →
    ∀ (pl : Pool) (sl : Slot), L.pools[j]? = some pl → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      ∀ r ∈ L.res, r.pool = pl.id → ∀ x, L.kern.Active x → (x = r.comp ∨ r.comp ∈ L.kern.ancs x) →
        ∀ l ∈ L.kern.afp x, l ∉ footprint L.kern.P sl.place

/-- `PoolInv` as the contract states it (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, as corrected; non-normative
library contract): entry disjointness, `pool_no_stale_access`, and the transition guarantee of
`freeSlot` (§55, §57). It is false on a library-reachable state
(`Witness.pool_inv_preserved_false`). -/
def PoolInv (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop := EntriesDisjoint L ∧ NoStale L ∧ FreeGuarantee k L

/-- Same-pool restriction of `PoolInv` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4; non-normative library
contract): items 1 and 2 as the contract states them, item 3 restricted to the companions of the
slot's pool (`FreeGuaranteeSamePool`). This is not the contract's statement (`PoolInv`) (§55,
§57). -/
def PoolInvSamePool (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop :=
  EntriesDisjoint L ∧ NoStale L ∧ FreeGuaranteeSamePool k L

/-- `EntriesDisjoint` follows from the ghost well-formedness (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 1)
(§40). -/
theorem entriesDisjoint_of {L : PState} (hwf : PoolWF L) : EntriesDisjoint L := by
  intro pl hpl
  have hok := hwf.pools _ (List.mem_map_of_mem hpl)
  exact ⟨fun sl hsl l hl => hok.slotIn sl.place (List.mem_map_of_mem (f := (·.place)) hsl) l hl,
    fun a b sa sb ha hb hab => hok.disjoint a b sa.place sb.place
      (by simp [Pool.shape, ha]) (by simp [Pool.shape, hb]) hab⟩

/-- The same-pool transition guarantee follows from the ghost well-formedness (HandlePool v0.4
annex, D.4, item 3, restricted to the slot's pool): an active descendant of a companion of the pool
is younger than `internal`, so it is neither `internal` nor one of its ancestors, and
`ContentEndPre` forbids it to cover the entry (§43, §69). -/
theorem freeGuaranteeSamePool_of {k : K} {L : PState} (hwf : PoolWF L) :
    FreeGuaranteeSamePool k L := by
  intro j h L' hst pl sl hpj hsl r hr hrp x hx hxr l hl hlq
  cases hst with
  | @ok pl' sl' hpj' _ _ hsl' hpre =>
    rw [hpj] at hpj'; cases hpj'
    rw [hsl] at hsl'; cases hsl'
    obtain ⟨hint, hlt, -, -⟩ := res_internal hwf hr (List.mem_of_getElem? hpj) hrp
    obtain ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ := hx
    have hex := hpre.entry x (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy)) ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ ⟨l, hl, hlq⟩
    have hcx : r.comp ≤ x := by
      rcases hxr with rfl | hc
      · exact Nat.le_refl _
      · exact Nat.le_of_lt (chain_lt hc)
    unfold Exempt at hex
    rcases hex with rfl | h'
    · omega
    · have := chain_lt h'; omega

/-- `pool_inv_preserved`, same-pool restriction (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4): `PoolInvSamePool`
holds on every state of a library run whose steps start from states satisfying `KInv` (§57); with
`PReach.toI`, on every library-reachable state under the guarantee of §57. This is not the
contract's statement: `PoolInv` is false on such a state (`Witness.pool_inv_preserved_false`). -/
theorem pool_inv_preserved_same_pool {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) : PoolInvSamePool k L :=
  have ⟨_, hwf, hns, _⟩ := pReachI_inv h
  ⟨entriesDisjoint_of hwf, hns, freeGuaranteeSamePool_of hwf⟩

/-- `pool_entries_disjoint` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 1; §40). -/
theorem pool_entries_disjoint {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    EntriesDisjoint L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved_same_pool h).1

/-- `pool_no_stale_access` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 2): on every state of a library run
(`PReachI`), an active entry authority designates a live slot at its current generation (§89). -/
theorem pool_no_stale_access {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    NoStale L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved_same_pool h).2.1

/-- `pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc`, same-pool restriction (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 3):
on every state of a library run (`PReachI`), `freeSlot` never succeeds while the companion of a
resolution of the pool, or an active descendant of it, covers the slot (§43, §69). This is not the
contract's statement: `FreeGuarantee` is false on such a state
(`Witness.pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_false`). -/
theorem pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_same_pool {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) : FreeGuaranteeSamePool k L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved_same_pool h).2.2

/-- Exclusivity of a `Modify` companion, as the contract states it (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2:
"Une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles compagnes sur l'intégralité du stockage du pool";
non-normative library contract): an active `Modify` companion of a pool is the only active
companion that covers a leaf of that pool's storage (§43, §50). The contract does not restrict the
other companions to the same pool. This property is false on a library-reachable state
(`Witness.pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_false`). -/
def ModifyExclusive (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ r₁ ∈ L.res, ∀ r₂ ∈ L.res, ∀ pl ∈ L.pools, r₁.pool = pl.id → L.kern.Active r₁.comp →
    L.kern.Active r₂.comp → r₁.mode = .modify →
    (∃ l ∈ L.kern.afp r₂.comp, l ∈ footprint L.kern.P pl.storage) → r₁.comp = r₂.comp

/-- `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive`, same-pool restriction (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2: "La
propriété d'exclusivité concerne toutes les suites d'opérations admises du noyau"): on every state
of a library run (`PReachI`), whatever its kernel steps, an active `Modify` companion of a pool is
the only active companion of that pool (§43, §50). This is not the contract's statement:
`ModifyExclusive`, which also covers the companions of other pools, is false on such a state
(`Witness.pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_false`). -/
theorem pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_same_pool {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    ∀ r₁ ∈ L.res, ∀ r₂ ∈ L.res, r₁.pool = r₂.pool → L.kern.Active r₁.comp →
      L.kern.Active r₂.comp → r₁.mode = .modify → r₁.comp = r₂.comp := by
  intro r₁ hr₁ r₂ hr₂ hp ha₁ ha₂ hm
  refine Decidable.byContradiction fun hne => ?_
  have := (pReachI_inv h).2.2.2 r₁ hr₁ r₂ hr₂ hp hne ha₁ ha₂
  rw [hm] at this; cases this.1
EOF

/-- `PoolInv`, item 3, the transition guarantee, as the contract states it (HandlePool v0.4 annex,
D.4: "`freeSlot` n'aboutit jamais si une descendante active d'une compagne couvre le slot
concerné"; non-normative library contract): `freeSlot` never succeeds while an active strict
descendant of a companion covers the slot concerned (§43, §69). The contract does not restrict the
companion to the pool of the slot. This guarantee is false on a library-reachable state
(`Witness.pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_false`): D.3 exempts "`internal` et ses ancêtres", which
may include a companion of another pool. -/
def FreeGuarantee (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (L' : PState), FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L') →
    ∀ (pl : Pool) (sl : Slot), L.pools[j]? = some pl → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      ∀ r ∈ L.res, ∀ x, L.kern.Active x → r.comp ∈ L.kern.ancs x →
        ∀ l ∈ L.kern.afp x, l ∉ footprint L.kern.P sl.place

/-- Same-pool restriction of the transition guarantee (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 3;
non-normative library contract). This is not the contract's statement (`FreeGuarantee`): only the
companions of the slot's pool are quantified (`r.pool = pl.id`). On that point it is weaker; it also
covers the companion itself, and on that point it is stronger (§43, §69). -/
def FreeGuaranteeSamePool (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (L' : PState), FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L') →
    ∀ (pl : Pool) (sl : Slot), L.pools[j]? = some pl → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      ∀ r ∈ L.res, r.pool = pl.id → ∀ x, L.kern.Active x → (x = r.comp ∨ r.comp ∈ L.kern.ancs x) →
        ∀ l ∈ L.kern.afp x, l ∉ footprint L.kern.P sl.place

/-- `PoolInv` as the contract states it (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, as corrected; non-normative
library contract): entry disjointness, `pool_no_stale_access`, and the transition guarantee of
`freeSlot` (§55, §57). It is false on a library-reachable state
(`Witness.pool_inv_preserved_false`). -/
def PoolInv (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop := EntriesDisjoint L ∧ NoStale L ∧ FreeGuarantee k L

/-- Same-pool restriction of `PoolInv` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4; non-normative library
contract): items 1 and 2 as the contract states them, item 3 restricted to the companions of the
slot's pool (`FreeGuaranteeSamePool`). This is not the contract's statement (`PoolInv`) (§55,
§57). -/
def PoolInvSamePool (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop :=
  EntriesDisjoint L ∧ NoStale L ∧ FreeGuaranteeSamePool k L

/-- `EntriesDisjoint` follows from the ghost well-formedness (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 1)
(§40). -/
theorem entriesDisjoint_of {L : PState} (hwf : PoolWF L) : EntriesDisjoint L := by
  intro pl hpl
  have hok := hwf.pools _ (List.mem_map_of_mem hpl)
  exact ⟨fun sl hsl l hl => hok.slotIn sl.place (List.mem_map_of_mem (f := (·.place)) hsl) l hl,
    fun a b sa sb ha hb hab => hok.disjoint a b sa.place sb.place
      (by simp [Pool.shape, ha]) (by simp [Pool.shape, hb]) hab⟩

/-- The same-pool transition guarantee follows from the ghost well-formedness (HandlePool v0.4
annex, D.4, item 3, restricted to the slot's pool): an active descendant of a companion of the pool
is younger than `internal`, so it is neither `internal` nor one of its ancestors, and
`ContentEndPre` forbids it to cover the entry (§43, §69). -/
theorem freeGuaranteeSamePool_of {k : K} {L : PState} (hwf : PoolWF L) :
    FreeGuaranteeSamePool k L := by
  intro j h L' hst pl sl hpj hsl r hr hrp x hx hxr l hl hlq
  cases hst with
  | @ok pl' sl' hpj' _ _ hsl' hpre =>
    rw [hpj] at hpj'; cases hpj'
    rw [hsl] at hsl'; cases hsl'
    obtain ⟨hint, hlt, -, -⟩ := res_internal hwf hr (List.mem_of_getElem? hpj) hrp
    obtain ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ := hx
    have hex := hpre.entry x (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy)) ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ ⟨l, hl, hlq⟩
    have hcx : r.comp ≤ x := by
      rcases hxr with rfl | hc
      · exact Nat.le_refl _
      · exact Nat.le_of_lt (chain_lt hc)
    unfold Exempt at hex
    rcases hex with rfl | h'
    · omega
    · have := chain_lt h'; omega

/-- `pool_inv_preserved`, same-pool restriction (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4): `PoolInvSamePool`
holds on every state of a library run whose steps start from states satisfying `KInv` (§57); with
`PReach.toI`, on every library-reachable state under the guarantee of §57. This is not the
contract's statement: `PoolInv` is false on such a state (`Witness.pool_inv_preserved_false`). -/
theorem pool_inv_preserved_same_pool {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) : PoolInvSamePool k L :=
  have ⟨_, hwf, hns, _⟩ := pReachI_inv h
  ⟨entriesDisjoint_of hwf, hns, freeGuaranteeSamePool_of hwf⟩

/-- `pool_entries_disjoint` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 1; §40). -/
theorem pool_entries_disjoint {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    EntriesDisjoint L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved_same_pool h).1

/-- `pool_no_stale_access` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 2): on every state of a library run
(`PReachI`), an active entry authority designates a live slot at its current generation (§89). -/
theorem pool_no_stale_access {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    NoStale L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved_same_pool h).2.1

/-- `pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc`, same-pool restriction (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 3):
on every state of a library run (`PReachI`), `freeSlot` never succeeds while the companion of a
resolution of the pool, or an active descendant of it, covers the slot (§43, §69). This is not the
contract's statement: `FreeGuarantee` is false on such a state
(`Witness.pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_false`). -/
theorem pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_same_pool {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) : FreeGuaranteeSamePool k L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved_same_pool h).2.2

/-- Exclusivity of a `Modify` companion, as the contract states it (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2:
"Une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles compagnes sur l'intégralité du stockage du pool";
non-normative library contract): an active `Modify` companion of a pool is the only active
companion that covers a leaf of that pool's storage (§43, §50). The contract does not restrict the
other companions to the same pool. This property is false on a library-reachable state
(`Witness.pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_false`). -/
def ModifyExclusive (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ r₁ ∈ L.res, ∀ r₂ ∈ L.res, ∀ pl ∈ L.pools, r₁.pool = pl.id → L.kern.Active r₁.comp →
    L.kern.Active r₂.comp → r₁.mode = .modify →
    (∃ l ∈ L.kern.afp r₂.comp, l ∈ footprint L.kern.P pl.storage) → r₁.comp = r₂.comp

/-- `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive`, same-pool restriction (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2: "La
propriété d'exclusivité concerne toutes les suites d'opérations admises du noyau"): on every state
of a library run (`PReachI`), whatever its kernel steps, an active `Modify` companion of a pool is
the only active companion of that pool (§43, §50). This is not the contract's statement:
`ModifyExclusive`, which also covers the companions of other pools, is false on such a state
(`Witness.pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_false`). -/
theorem pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_same_pool {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    ∀ r₁ ∈ L.res, ∀ r₂ ∈ L.res, r₁.pool = r₂.pool → L.kern.Active r₁.comp →
      L.kern.Active r₂.comp → r₁.mode = .modify → r₁.comp = r₂.comp := by
  intro r₁ hr₁ r₂ hr₂ hp ha₁ ha₂ hm
  refine Decidable.byContradiction fun hne => ?_
  have := (pReachI_inv h).2.2.2 r₁ hr₁ r₂ hr₂ hp hne ha₁ ha₂
  rw [hm] at this; cases this.1
